title: India Beat Pakistan by 19 Runs to Defend Asian Games Cricket Gold
excerpt: Abhishek Sharma's 61 and Tilak Varma's unbeaten 51 powered India to 211/6 before the spinners held off Hasan Nawaz's 96 in a 19-run final win at Nisshin.
body:
• India defended their Asian Games men's cricket gold with a 19-run win over Pakistan in the final at Nisshin, Japan, on October 3, 2026 — settling on the field what the rain-affected 2023 final decided on rankings.
  • Abhishek Sharma (61 off 28) and Tilak Varma (51* off 22) powered India to 211/6; Hasan Nawaz's 51-ball 96 gave Pakistan hope before India's spinners closed out a 192/6 chase.
  • The result gives India a 4-3 edge over Pakistan in finals of major tournaments, and comes two years before cricket returns to the Olympics at Los Angeles 2028.
  • The win was part of a golden Day 15 for India: the men's hockey team also defended its Asian title 5-1 over Malaysia, sealing direct LA 2028 qualification alongside the women's champions.

India defended their Asian Games men's cricket gold medal on Saturday, beating Pakistan by 19 runs in a tense final at Nisshin, Japan. Rapid half-centuries from Abhishek Sharma and Tilak Varma, backed by controlled spin bowling at the death, secured the title before a watching subcontinent — and settled on the field what the rain-affected 2023 final had decided on ICC rankings.

The final

India won the toss and batted, posting 211/6 in 20 overs. Abhishek gave the innings its flying start — 61 off 28 balls with 7 sixes — and Tilak provided the finish, an unbeaten 51 off 22 balls with a blistering 62-run death partnership alongside Shivam Dube (27 off 15). For Pakistan, Arafat Minhas (3-25) and Ahmed Daniyal (2-43) were the pick of the bowlers.

""A huge occasion when you are playing Pakistan in the final, the whole country is watching and you have that pressure," India captain Shreyas Iyer said afterward, per Reuters."

The chase hinged on Hasan Nawaz. The Pakistan batter produced a stunning 51-ball 96 that turned a routine defence into a tense finish — but with 44 needed off 12 balls, India's bowlers held their nerve. Axar Patel (2-29), Washington Sundar (2-29) and Dube (2-33) shared the damage as Pakistan closed on 192/6. "A huge occasion when you are playing Pakistan in the final, the whole country is watching and you have that pressure," India captain Shreyas Iyer said afterward, per Reuters.

Context: a rivalry beyond the boundary

The final pitted a full-strength India against a second-string Pakistan, and for two-thirds of the contest it went to script — but Nawaz's assault ensured the game lived up to the billing of the sport's fiercest rivalry. This was also the backdrop of the "no handshake" protocol that had marked India-Pakistan encounters through the tournament, a visible sign of the political chill between the two countries bleeding into sport.

It was a more satisfying defence than the 2023 Hangzhou title, which India won without bowling a ball in a washed-out final against Afghanistan — decided on T20I rankings. Per Cricinfo, India now hold a 4-3 advantage over Pakistan in finals of multi-team tournaments across formats.

Diaspora angle

For the diaspora, this was the rare sporting event that froze two time zones at once — morning in the US, evening in India — with family WhatsApp groups doing double duty as commentary boxes. The win also keeps India on track for Los Angeles 2028, where cricket returns to the Olympics and the diaspora will be among the loudest in the stands. The women's team, already gold medallists, completed India's cricket double earlier in the week.

What's next

The gold took India's Asian Games 2026 tally to the mid-80s, with the men's hockey team joining cricket on the podium on Day 15 — Harmanpreet Singh scoring twice in a 5-1 rout of Malaysia for back-to-back titles and direct Olympic qualification. With one day of competition remaining, India's fourth-place finish on the medal table was effectively sealed — and the cricket gold, won outright on the field against Pakistan, will be the image the Games are remembered by.
